extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and teams applying for CDMRP funding opportunities (grant applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) two-tier application review process (peer review then programmatic review), the criteria used at each tier, scoring conventions, and applicant-facing expectations for preparing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review — scientific and technical merit (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first tier is peer review: a criteria-based process where your application is individually evaluated based on its scientific and technical merit relative to an ideal application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The outcome is an overall merit score used to assess application quality. Applicants should write to maximize scientific/technical merit as judged against the ideal application described by the funding opportunity's evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review — specific evaluation criteria (scored criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers use specific evaluation criteria described in each funding opportunity; applicants can use the evaluation criteria as a rubric to guide application writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most important peer review criteria receive individual scores (scale 1–10, whole numbers). Applicants should follow the FOA's listed criteria and structure content to directly address each scored criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unscored peer review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding opportunities describe both scored and unscored criteria. Although the unscored criteria do not receive individual criterion scores, peer reviewers do factor those criteria into the overall scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a criterion is unscored, address it clearly because it may influence the panel discussion and the overall merit score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting or ordering of scored criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should note whether the scored criteria are weighted equally or whether the criteria are listed in descending order of importance and take this into consideration when composing their applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate effort and page space according to the FOA's indicated weighting/ordering of criteria (e.g., emphasize higher-weighted criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay abstract and impact statements (consumer-facing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer reviewers rely heavily on the lay abstract and the impact statements; CDMRP uses 'consumers' to refer to survivors, persons living with, family members, or caregivers of individuals with the disease/injury/condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly describe the proposed research and anticipated impact in language accessible to non-scientists; these components are critical for consumer assessment of potential impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review panel composition and recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: CDMRP programs recruit peer reviewers after receipt of full applications; there are no standing panels. Panels include the experts needed that fiscal year (scientists, clinicians, consumers, specialists as needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect panel makeup to reflect the applications received; you will not know individual reviewers' identities (policy prohibits contact). Program staff publish lists of peer reviewers after peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement content and role
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome from peer review is the Summary Statement, which includes a score for overall merit, individual evaluation scores, and a written critique of strengths and weaknesses; discussion notes may also be captured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Summary Statement is both the primary feedback for applicants and an input to programmatic review. Use it to understand critiques and strengths, but programmatic reviewers will also rely on it when making funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score scale (peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application receives an overall score representing overall assessment of merit. Scores range between 1 and 5, with 1 representing the highest merit and 5 the lowest merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall scores are averaged among panel members and reported on the first page of the Summary Statement; understand that lower numbers represent better merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual criterion scoring scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual evaluation criteria (the most important ones) receive scores from each reviewer using a scale of 1 to 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On this scale 1 represents the lowest merit and 10 the highest merit; whole numbers only. These per-criterion scores are reported in the Summary Statement and inform the overall assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic review — comparison-based assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The second tier is programmatic review: a comparison-based process where the highest scoring applications from peer review are assessed against the programmatic review criteria described in the funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic reviewers compare applications to each other (not re-review scientific merit). They may only receive the Summary Statement, Abstract, and selected attachments necessary to assess programmatic criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic review criteria (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic review criteria may include considerations such as adherence to the intent of the mechanism, relative innovation and/or impact compared to the other applications under consideration, relevance to program goals, and consideration of portfolio composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address not only scientific merit but also how your project fits the mechanism's intent, contributes innovation/impact relative to other possible projects, and complements the program's desired portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic portfolio balance and investment strategy alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The programmatic panel aims to recommend a broad portfolio of applications for funding that aligns with the investment strategy for the program cycle and reflects the program's priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High peer-review scores do not guarantee funding; programmatic priorities, portfolio balance, and investment strategy influence final recommendations (CDMRP does not use a pay line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate lists and final approval/notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic panels may compose an 'alternate list' of awards not initially recommended; alternates may be reconsidered if funds become available. Once recommendations receive final approval, applicants are notified approximately three to six weeks after programmatic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receive the Summary Statement and an information paper with funding metrics at notification. Unfunded applicants receive brief feedback on the primary reason they were not selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application preparation — follow FOA instructions exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: When working on your application, carefully follow the instructions in the funding opportunity and include the correct information within the correct application component/attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDMRP does not provide one-on-one guidance about whether a project fits program interests. The FOA and general application instructions contain all information applicants need; follow them precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and prior-application consideration policy
rubrics_metrics.description: CDMRP does not operate a resubmission process where reviewers consider prior submissions. Applications revised and submitted to future opportunities are treated as new applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect prior reviews to be considered; if you re-submit to a future FOA, address the current FOA's requirements and treat the submission as an independent application.
